# Stereo models

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_docs.py from the model cards; do not edit. -->

71 stereo models. Each section says what the model is, whether it may be used commercially and how fast it is; licences and checks are under Details.

Input: a rectified left / right image pair. Output: a disparity map (pixels, left view).

Measured on RTX 5060 Ti, torch 2.14.1+cu130; `fastforks bench MODEL --size HxW` measures yours. The summary uses one input, 994x1482: kernels time with its speed-up over the faster original run, and kernels peak reserved memory with its ratio to the smaller original one. Where measured (one variant per family), a variant's table also lists portable under `torch.compile` and the fp16 TensorRT engine of portable ([export](../export.md); memory: the engine's device memory). – = not measured. The accuracy column is lower-is-better (ETH3D bad > 1 px (%)).

Other devices: [Apple M1 Pro 16 GB](../devices/apple-m1-pro-16gb.md), [NVIDIA L4](../devices/l4-22gb.md), [NVIDIA L40S](../devices/l40s-44gb.md), [NVIDIA A10](../devices/a10-22gb.md), [NVIDIA A100-SXM4-40GB](../devices/a100-sxm4-40gb.md), [NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000](../devices/rtx-pro-6000-96gb.md); [across devices](../benchmarks.md#other-devices).

<a id="aanet"></a>

## AANet

A stereo network that aggregates matching costs with sparse deformable sampling across scales, trained on synthetic SceneFlow data.

Commercial use: yes.

| variant | input | backend | time (ms) | peak memory (MiB, allocated / reserved) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `aanet-sceneflow` | Middlebury 2014 half (994x1482) | original (fp32)<br>original<br>portable<br>kernels<br>portable + torch.compile<br>TensorRT fp16 | 289<br>178<br>140<br>101<br>91.8<br>91.2 | 1785 / 1962<br>1000 / 1126<br>845 / 986<br>536 / 644<br>754 / 928<br>482 (engine) |
| `aanet-plus-sceneflow` | Middlebury 2014 half (994x1482) | original (fp32)<br>original<br>portable<br>kernels | 263<br>194<br>159<br>88.9 | 3618 / 3896<br>3652 / 3784<br>1142 / 1278<br>813 / 920 |

<details><summary>Details</summary>

- Paper: [AANet: Adaptive Aggregation Network for Efficient Stereo Matching](https://arxiv.org/abs/2004.09548), CVPR 2020, 2020-04-20
- Original code: <https://github.com/haofeixu/aanet> at `8d0d747e69bb`
- Code licence: Apache-2.0 (permissive); files: `LICENSE`
- Weights licence: Apache-2.0 (assumed from code)
- Licence evidence: <https://github.com/haofeixu/aanet/blob/8d0d747e69bbdba43e2578b60ad7df63ba7fdac2/LICENSE>
- Training data: Freiburg SceneFlow (FlyingThings3D, Driving, Monkaa)
- Kernel libraries: `deform_conv`, `igev`, `cutlass_conv`, `cudnn_hacc`
- Variants: `aanet-sceneflow`, `aanet-plus-sceneflow`
- Outputs: disparity
- Input size:
  - `aanet-sceneflow`: any H x W >= 48, padded to a multiple of 48
  - `aanet-plus-sceneflow`: any H x W >= 96, padded to a multiple of 96
- Tested up to (portable, fp16, RTX 5060 Ti 16 GB): `aanet-sceneflow` 3000x4000 (9.4 GiB peak allocated, 12.5 reserved); `aanet-plus-sceneflow` 1024x2048 (7.1 GiB peak allocated, 8.1 reserved)
- `aanet-sceneflow` 994x1482, first call: portable + torch.compile 80 s (cold Inductor cache), TensorRT fp16 211 s (ONNX + engine).
- `aanet-sceneflow` original (fp32) 994x1482: deformable conv via torchvision.ops.deform_conv2d (original CUDA extension not built)
- `aanet-sceneflow` original 994x1482: torch.autocast(fp16) around the forward; deformable conv via torchvision.ops.deform_conv2d (original CUDA extension not built)
- `aanet-plus-sceneflow` original (fp32) 994x1482: deformable conv via torchvision.ops.deform_conv2d (original CUDA extension not built)
- `aanet-plus-sceneflow` original 994x1482: torch.autocast(fp16) around the forward; deformable conv via torchvision.ops.deform_conv2d (original CUDA extension not built)
- `aanet-sceneflow` load / first call: original 0.12 s / 0.067 s (375x1242), portable 0.19 s / 0.143† s, kernels 0.27† s / 0.101† s
- `aanet-plus-sceneflow` load / first call: original 0.15 s / 0.701 s (375x1242), portable 0.16 s / 0.166† s, kernels 0.2† s / 0.09† s
- † measured in the speed sweep after the portable load (or an earlier size) in the same process: file cache and kernels are warm, so the time is lower than a fresh start.
- Protocol, median of 5 after 3 warm-up, uint8 CUDA input (synthetic for bench_inputs sizes), card defaults; gc before each load; peak = max over the first call and the timed calls

### Measured

Original = the original code named under Details, same checkpoint and protocol.

| variant | dataset | original fp32 | original fp16 | portable | kernels | note |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `aanet-sceneflow` | ETH3D two-view train, bad > 1 px % / EPE | 14.64 / 0.697 | 14.63 / 0.697 | 14.63 / 0.697 | 14.64 / 0.698 |  |
| `aanet-sceneflow` | Middlebury 2014 trainingH, bad > 2 px % / EPE | 32.15 / 6.305 | 32.15 / 6.301 | 32.16 / 6.301 | 32.16 / 6.303 |  |
| `aanet-plus-sceneflow` | ETH3D two-view train, bad > 1 px % / EPE | 18.48 / 0.811 | 18.50 / 0.812 | 18.50 / 0.811 | 18.50 / 0.812 |  |
| `aanet-plus-sceneflow` | Middlebury 2014 trainingH, bad > 2 px % / EPE | 29.84 / 6.237 | 29.85 / 6.236 | 29.86 / 6.237 | 29.86 / 6.232 |  |

Measured on NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5060 Ti, torch 2.14.1+cu130, fastforks 468fba10, 2026-11-05.

### Parity

CPU, float32: max |diff| <= 0.002 vs the original. GPU, float16 (the default), portable and kernels: mean |diff| <= 0.02 px and p99 <= 0.25 px.

| variant | kernels error vs original, mean / p99 | GPU, torch | kernels used |
|---|---|---|---|
| `aanet-sceneflow` | 0.00403 / 0.04845 | RTX 5060 Ti, torch 2.14.1+cu130 | `cudnn_hacc@cudnn92400`, `cutlass_conv@988138e042cb:sm_120`, `deform_conv@a38662ea1bfc:sm_120`, `igev@f075827d68c6:sm_120` |
| `aanet-plus-sceneflow` | 0.00295 / 0.02185 | RTX 5060 Ti, torch 2.14.1+cu130 | `cudnn_hacc@cudnn92400`, `cutlass_conv@988138e042cb:sm_120`, `deform_conv@a38662ea1bfc:sm_120`, `igev@f075827d68c6:sm_120` |

### Limitations

- Only the SceneFlow checkpoints of AANet and AANet+ are included; the original code's KITTI fine-tunes are not.
- At 375x1242 AANet is launch-bound: portable is about as fast as the original code. At 994x1482 portable is faster but allocates more memory.

</details>

## BridgeDepth

A stereo network that aligns Depth Anything V2 features with NMRF-style disparity proposals. Non-commercial weights.

Commercial use: **no** (weights: CC-BY-NC-4.0).

| variant | input | backend | time (ms) | peak memory (MiB, allocated / reserved) |
|---|---|---|---|---|

| `bridgedepth-rvc-pretrain` | Middlebury 2014 half (994x1482) | original (fp32)<br>original<br>portable<br>kernels | 629<br>470<br>442<br>354 | 2903 / 3178<br>2903 / 3200<br>2968 / 3246<br>2361 / 2686 |

For commercial use take c-foundationstereo-s (its model card says 'ready for commercial use').

A stereo network from the Insta360 Research Team that uses Depth Anything V2 features and an initial depth prior. Non-commercial weights.

Commercial use: **no** (weights: CC-BY-NC-4.0).

| variant | input | backend | time (ms) | peak memory (MiB, allocated / reserved) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `defom-stereo-vitl-sceneflow` | Middlebury 2014 half (994x1482) | original (fp32)<br>original<br>portable<br>kernels<br>portable + torch.compile<br>TensorRT fp16 | 4175<br>2816<br>1531<br>659<br>1002<br>fails: TensorRT bug: Myelin internal error | 10896 / 11072<br>8639 / 8766<br>4362 / 4838<br>3154 / 3566<br>3021 / 3292<br>– |

<details><summary>Details</summary>

- Paper: [DEFOM-Stereo: Depth Foundation Model Based Stereo Matching](https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.09466), CVPR 2025, 2025-01-16
- Original code: <https://github.com/Insta360-Research-Team/DEFOM-Stereo> at `5b27591d8395`
- Code licence: MIT (permissive); files: `LICENSE`
- Weights licence: CC-BY-NC-4.0
- Licence evidence: <https://github.com/Insta360-Research-Team/DEFOM-Stereo/blob/5b27591d83956e5d329ff66704271a9e68b1c75f/README.md>
- Training data: Freiburg SceneFlow (FlyingThings3D, Driving, Monkaa)
- Licence note: The weights embed Depth Anything V2 ViT-L weights released under CC-BY-NC-4.0, so they are non-commercial even though the code is MIT.
- Options: `iters` = 32 (>= 1), `scale_iters` = 8 (>= 0)
- Kernel libraries: `igev`, `cutlass_conv`, `cudnn_hacc`, `fastbb`
- Variants: `defom-stereo-vitl-sceneflow`
- Outputs: disparity
- Input size: any H x W >= 32, padded to a multiple of 32
- Tested up to (portable, fp16, RTX 5060 Ti 16 GB): `defom-stereo-vitl-sceneflow` 1988x2880 (12.0 GiB peak allocated, 14.5 reserved)
- `defom-stereo-vitl-sceneflow` 994x1482, first call: portable + torch.compile 122 s (cold Inductor cache).
- `defom-stereo-vitl-sceneflow` original 994x1482: the authors' mixed-precision option (float16)
- `defom-stereo-vitl-sceneflow` load / first call: original 4.24 s / 2.83 s, portable 2.31 s / 1.534† s, kernels 1.18† s / 0.663† s
- † measured in the speed sweep after the portable load (or an earlier size) in the same process: file cache and kernels are warm, so the time is lower than a fresh start.
- Protocol, median of 5 after 3 warm-up, uint8 CUDA input (synthetic for bench_inputs sizes), card defaults; gc before each load; peak = max over the first call and the timed calls

### Measured

Original = the original code named under Details, same checkpoint and protocol.

| variant | dataset | original fp32 | original fp16 | portable | kernels | note |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `defom-stereo-vitl-sceneflow` | ETH3D two-view train, bad > 1 px % / EPE | 2.40 / 0.337 | 99.92 / 13.132 (NaN / inf output) | 2.37 / 0.356 | 2.44 / 0.341 |  |
| `defom-stereo-vitl-sceneflow` | Middlebury 2014 trainingH, bad > 2 px % / EPE | 6.03 / 0.837 | 100.00 / 71.272 (NaN / inf output) | 6.15 / 0.845 | 6.02 / 0.834 |  |

Measured on NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5060 Ti, torch 2.14.1+cu130, fastforks 468fba10, 2026-11-05.

### Parity

CPU, float32: max |diff| <= 0.002 vs the original. GPU, portable bfloat16 and kernels float16 (the defaults): mean |diff| <= 0.02 px and p99 <= 0.25 px.

| variant | kernels error vs original, mean / p99 | GPU, torch | kernels used |
|---|---|---|---|
| `defom-stereo-vitl-sceneflow` | 0.00143 / 0.00808 | RTX 5060 Ti, torch 2.14.1+cu130 | `cudnn_hacc@cudnn92400`, `cutlass_conv@988138e042cb:sm_120`, `fastbb@7d058322634d:sm_120`, `igev@f075827d68c6:sm_120` |

### Limitations

- Only the ViT-L SceneFlow checkpoint is included (ViT-S / ViT-B and the Middlebury / ETH3D / KITTI fine-tunes are not).
- Portable is faster than the original code but allocates more memory (about 1.25x at 994x1482); kernels is several times faster and needs a fraction of the memory.

</details>

- The weights are the authors' frozen TensorFlow graphs read without TensorFlow; the FlyingThings and Middlebury d160 / d288 graphs are not included.

## WAFT-Stereo

A stereo network from the Princeton Vision & Learning Lab that warps features instead of building a cost volume, in sizes S and B. The licence differs by size, see the table.

Commercial use: `waft-stereo-s`: yes; `waft-stereo-b`: **no** (weights: CC-BY-NC-4.0).

| variant | input | backend | time (ms) | peak memory (MiB, allocated / reserved) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `waft-stereo-s` | Middlebury 2014 half (994x1482) | original (fp32)<br>original<br>portable<br>kernels<br>portable + torch.compile<br>TensorRT fp16 | 1252<br>689<br>689<br>284<br>357<br>170 | 3764 / 4352<br>3314 / 3398<br>3293 / 3456<br>1113 / 1286<br>2024 / 2058<br>662 (engine) |
| `waft-stereo-b` | Middlebury 2014 half (994x1482) | original (fp32)<br>original<br>portable<br>kernels | 1898<br>1140<br>1137<br>393 | 7348 / 7528<br>5743 / 5876<br>5775 / 5852<br>1907 / 2316 |

<details><summary>Details</summary>

- Paper: [WAFT-Stereo: Warping-Alone Field Transforms for Stereo Matching](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.24836), arXiv, 2026-03-25
- Original code: <https://github.com/princeton-vl/WAFT-Stereo> at `c534320860f4`
- Code licence: BSD-3-Clause (permissive); files: `LICENSE`
- Weights licence: BSD-3-Clause
  - `waft-stereo-b`: CC-BY-NC-4.0
- Licence evidence: https://github.com/princeton-vl/WAFT-Stereo/blob/c534320860f4bbb2c0df896e3ccb95de49284aec/LICENSE; vendored files (net/*.py) checked against c534320: none carries an NVIDIA or FoundationStereo header, original only credits FoundationStereo in its README, so BSD-3-Clause holds
- Training data: Freiburg SceneFlow (FlyingThings3D, Driving, Monkaa), not stated by the authors (SceneFlow, TartanAir, CREStereo, Falling Things, Sintel, Virtual KITTI 2, UnrealStereo4K, WMGStereo, CARLA, Spring, TartanGround, FSD (configs/SynLarge/*.yaml); only SceneFlow is in datasets.toml)
- Licence note: WAFT-Stereo-B is labelled CC-BY-NC-4.0 conservatively although the Hugging Face card says BSD-3-Clause: the checkpoint embeds a fine-tuned Depth Anything V2 ViT-B whose original weights are CC-BY-NC-4.0.
- Licence note: Both checkpoints were trained on data that includes NVIDIA's FSD dataset, whose terms for commercial use of trained models are unclear; the status does not depend on the training data.
- Kernel libraries: `igev`, `cutlass_conv`, `cudnn_hacc`, `fastbb`
- Variants: `waft-stereo-s`, `waft-stereo-b`
- Outputs: disparity
- Input size: any H x W >= 17, resized or padded inside the model
- Tested up to (portable, fp16, RTX 5060 Ti 16 GB): `waft-stereo-s` 1024x2048 (5.3 GiB peak allocated, 8.3 reserved); `waft-stereo-b` 1024x1024 (3.2 GiB peak allocated, 4.7 reserved)
- `waft-stereo-s` 994x1482, first call: portable + torch.compile 95 s (cold Inductor cache), TensorRT fp16 152 s (ONNX + engine).
- `waft-stereo-s` original 994x1482: torch.autocast(fp16) around the forward
- `waft-stereo-b` original 994x1482: torch.autocast(fp16) around the forward
- `waft-stereo-s` load / first call: original 1.6 s / 0.14 s (375x1242), portable 0.58 s / 0.691† s, kernels 0.3† s / 0.284† s
- `waft-stereo-b` load / first call: original 3.07 s / 0.444 s (375x1242), portable 1.65 s / 1.148† s, kernels 0.42† s / 0.393† s
- † measured in the speed sweep after the portable load (or an earlier size) in the same process: file cache and kernels are warm, so the time is lower than a fresh start.
- Protocol, median of 5 after 3 warm-up, uint8 CUDA input (synthetic for bench_inputs sizes), card defaults; gc before each load; peak = max over the first call and the timed calls

### Measured

Original = the original code named under Details, same checkpoint and protocol.

| variant | dataset | original fp32 | original fp16 | portable | kernels | note |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `waft-stereo-s` | ETH3D two-view train, bad > 1 px % / EPE | 0.95 / 0.177 | 0.95 / 0.177 | 0.95 / 0.177 | 0.95 / 0.177 | possibly in the training data |
| `waft-stereo-s` | Middlebury 2014 trainingH, bad > 2 px % / EPE | 4.75 / 0.895 | 4.74 / 0.895 | 4.75 / 0.895 | 4.77 / 0.897 | possibly in the training data |
| `waft-stereo-b` | ETH3D two-view train, bad > 1 px % / EPE | 0.74 / 0.163 | 0.74 / 0.163 | 0.74 / 0.163 | 0.74 / 0.163 | possibly in the training data |
| `waft-stereo-b` | Middlebury 2014 trainingH, bad > 2 px % / EPE | 3.38 / 0.728 | 3.39 / 0.728 | 3.38 / 0.729 | 3.38 / 0.728 | possibly in the training data |

Measured on NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5060 Ti, torch 2.14.1+cu130, fastforks 468fba10, 2026-11-05.

### Parity

CPU, float32: max |diff| <= 0.002 vs the original. GPU, float16 (the default), portable and kernels: mean |diff| <= 0.02 px and p99 <= 0.25 px.

| variant | kernels error vs original, mean / p99 | GPU, torch | kernels used |
|---|---|---|---|
| `waft-stereo-s` | 0.0013 / 0.00398 | RTX 5060 Ti, torch 2.14.1+cu130 | `cudnn_hacc@cudnn92400`, `cutlass_conv@988138e042cb:sm_120`, `fastbb@7d058322634d:sm_120`, `igev@f075827d68c6:sm_120` |
| `waft-stereo-b` | 0.0013 / 0.00417 | RTX 5060 Ti, torch 2.14.1+cu130 | `cudnn_hacc@cudnn92400`, `cutlass_conv@988138e042cb:sm_120`, `fastbb@7d058322634d:sm_120`, `igev@f075827d68c6:sm_120` |

### Limitations

- Only the two SynLarge checkpoints (S, B) are included; DAv2L-5 and the Real / KITTI / Middlebury fine-tunes are not.
- Portable WAFT-B is slightly slower than the original code and allocates slightly more memory; kernels is about 3x faster with a third of the memory.
- WAFT-Stereo-B kernels runs its ViT attention with fp16 accumulation: single attention outputs differ from fp32 by up to 34 % (relative), but end-to-end ETH3D / Middlebury-H accuracy matches the fp32 original (EPE 0.163 / 0.728).

</details>
